clash_scan.scope: all 272 non-wire parts pairwise (solid intersection > 0.05 mm3; the bumper halves are modelled with the leaf deflected onto its abutment, so P_base is no longer exempt); fasteners, inserts, races and moving hardware by minimum gap; wires by minimum gap (>= 0.3 mm to every non-terminal part)

fastener_clearances.note: Static fasteners, inserts, nuts, module screws, standoffs, dowels, base races and switch bodies vs every part they are not designed to touch: >= 0.5 mm; moving pins, bearings, springs, riders, races and balls (5 positions) and the moving halves: >= 2.0 mm to parts, >= 1.0 mm to wires; rigid half to P_base >= 1.0 mm at every travel; base races to moving parts >= 0.7 mm; switch body vs moving half >= 1.0 mm; leaf vs switch >= 1.0 mm, leaf body vs its abutment >= 0.3 mm, leaf abutment vs switch >= 1.0 mm.

blind_pilots.rule: thread-forming screws >= 5 mm engagement in PETG; machine screws >= 2.5 mm (5 threads) inside a brass insert; tips from below >= 0.8 mm inside the base top

carrier_lead_tail_slab.note: the Jetson carrier footprint, z 54.77..57 (2.23 mm of through-hole lead tails): only the Jetson and its standoff stacks may enter it

wire_to_wire.scope: motor-side bundle (pigtails, factory cables and every lead within 5 mm of them) at >= required_mm; every other pair within 5 mm: no interpenetration

envelope.about: z axis through base_link (0,0) = drive axle

planar_play.method: every mesh vertex of the left half and its foam (the right half is its mirror image) over every feasible pose

planar_play_with_tilt.method: skin sample points (every 2 deg, z 26/70/114 and the rim) tilted by every vertex of the stop-gap tilt set, then moved by every feasible planar pose

print_tolerance_mm.note: checked with a printed radius template before the foam is bonded; foam measured 1.5 ± 0.2

envelope.turn_in_place_note: The axle is the circle centre, so a spin in place sweeps exactly this circle.

bumper_travel.guide_angle_note: inward of rearward: left half moves along (-cos30, -sin30), right half along (-cos30, +sin30)

vertical_guide.type: rolling Ø4 balls between 0.5 mm hardened spring-steel races, spring-preloaded
vertical_guide.tolerance_note: The half is pulled up against its three down balls by the pin springs, so its attitude is set by the base underside and three metal heights; the printed base thickness (±0.15) and pocket depths (±0.1) move the rider up or down by at most ±0.25 mm, which only changes the spring length by the same amount (preload ±0.5 N) because the 0.1 mm stop gap is set with a feeler at assembly. Rider-to-race running clearance 1.0 ± 0.25 mm; clamp nut to rider counterbore 0.4 ± 0.25 mm.

planar_play.pose: (s, e, phi): travel along the half axis, sideways shift along its normal, yaw about rail pin A; feasible when both bearing centres lie inside their slot stadiums
planar_play.hard_stop_note: The hard stop is at s = 5.0 with the bearing centred and 4.9 mm with it on a slot side; rest is s = 0 (centred) to 0.1.

seam.grid_note: key "t1,t2": left travel, right travel (mm), nominal (no side play)
seam.tongue: Right-half backer: one flat step facing +x at x 148.32 across the seam (y -4.35..+3.75), 2.3 mm (design) from the region swept by the left end inner corner over every (t1, t2), joined to the right wall by a web behind the right end.

seam_intrusion.rod: round Ø3 flat-ended rod, 9 ray samples over its section, centres y -4..+4, pushed along -x
seam_intrusion.trip_rule: (-n).t - 0.5 |(-n).normal| >= 0.3 at the first contact face; rod advance per mm of travel = (t.n)/(d.n); trip at 2.25 mm of travel
seam_intrusion.limit_note: A rod narrower than the 7.5 mm seam passes between the seam-end ramps and meets the backer step (normal +x, drive 0.87), which must stay 2.3 mm (design) behind the region the left end sweeps: that sets the deepest unsensed intrusion of thin objects at the seam (max_intrusion_before_trip_mm). Wider objects meet a ramp or the skin first.

nose_contact.method: deflected constant-strength leaf integrated with large slopes; the projected length shortens as it bends, pulling the Ø4 nose toward the root; side play moves it 1:1 along the leaf axis, yaw about pin A a little more

leaf_spring.note: Tip-loaded cantilever integrated over the parabolic section from the root-boss edge (the one-sided R1.5 fillet adds a little stiffness and is ignored). Printed upright with the half, so the leaf bends within its layers; the Ø4 nose bears on a P_base abutment whose face is normal to the travel. 35 % relaxation is assumed for PETG at the 5 MPa rest stress over the product life. The worst case (E 1700, leaf 0.05 mm thin, 35 % creep) still returns the half with >= 0.5 N.

switch.model: Omron SS-5GL2 (hinge roller lever, Ø4.8 roller on a 14.5 mm lever)

datasheet.source: Omron SS subminiature basic switch datasheet (en-ss.pdf), hinge roller lever table; heights of the roller top above the mounting-hole line

switch.calibration: OP tolerance (±0.8 mm) exceeds OT min (1.2 mm), so the switch slides ±0.9 mm in slotted P_base holes and is set at assembly to operate at 2.25 mm of travel (gauge block at the rest stop) while the roller force holds the bearing on its slot side. During a hit the bearing may sit on the other side of the slot (2 × side play), which makes the switch operate earlier, never later.

cam.note: The round Ø4.8 roller meets the 40 deg ramp line almost at once (lever moves from about s 0); there is no dead band.

slot_width_cases.bearing_contact: one side at a time: rolls
one side at a time: rolls
one side at a time: rolls

switch.roller_force_on_half: At most OF 0.49 N along +Y (the half's +nrm direction): a light, constant side bias.
switch.dog_direction_note: The cam approaches the roller from the lever-tip side (cam normal 54-62 deg from the roller path); the Omron SS datasheet text available has no dog-direction rule: confirm with Omron's basic-switch precautions before release.

preload_balance.note: The half hangs on three springs that pull it up against three down balls; at rest it cannot tilt inside any clearance. Riders and their balls rest on the base, not on the half.

tilt_under_load.note: Only under a load larger than the preload (a hit high on the skin): the half tilts within the 0.1 mm stop gap and the 0.4 mm clamp-nut gap. At rest the springs hold the nominal pose.

friction_lock.method: Quasi-static rigid half; lateral reactions at the two rail-pin bearings; vertical reactions at the 9 ball contacts shared as a compliant body (equal stiffness, unilateral, minimum-norm), friction moments iterated. mu_vert_crit = vertical-contact friction at which a hit stops sliding the half (larger is better).
friction_lock.design_case: rolling balls mu 0.03 (conservative for steel races), 693ZZ bearings mu 0.03, frictionless contact
friction_lock.one_ball_note: The single most loaded ball at each hit seized and sliding at mu 0.15 on its steel race (the others rolling): a partial failure the design must still sense.
friction_lock.races_note: Every ball runs between hardened steel strips (no PETG contact, no dimpling: see hertz). The sliding case is a failure mode (a ball seized in its pocket), not the design.
friction_lock.object_friction_note: Static or side pushes: the skin slides along the object as the half moves along its 30 deg axis; EVA foam mu_c as stated on az < 70, PTFE-taped PETG (mu_c 0.2) on az 70..90.
friction_lock.heights_note: Full height 98.5 (97.3 on the seam band chamfer); heights inside the camera window (|az| < 8.0 deg) are skipped; every listed height has bumper surface.

hertz.ball_race: 0.5 mm hardened spring steel (blue-tempered 1095 or AISI 420, >= HRC 48) on every ball face; Ø4 G10 52100 balls
hertz.note: Ball faces are steel on both sides; PETG only carries the spread load of the strip. The bearing outer race rolls on the PETG slot side (line contact): reported against the same 40 MPa limit.
hertz.stall_note: At a 14 N wheel-stall push held at the hard stop the most loaded ball reaches the p0 above: hardened (>= HRC 55) races may take micrometre brinell marks there; inspect the races at service. PETG faces stay under 40 MPa even then.

trip_force_N.return_note: On the return stroke the roller pushes the cam back (helps); only the race rolling drag resists.

bumper_travel.intended_contacts: Balls roll between steel races (pocket floor / rider ceiling and the strips bonded to P_base); the rail-pin bearings roll in the P_base slots; the preloaded leaf nose bears on the P_base abutment; the cam holds the switch roller (pre-pressed at rest).

perimeter_rod_intrusion.rod: Ø3 flat-ended rod (9 ray samples), radial, every 0.5 deg
perimeter_rod_intrusion.rule: first contact P_bumper_*/bumper_foam_* (sensed) or P_rear_shell_* (or the flush round-lid rim behind the bumper span, |az| > 90) within 13.6 mm

lid_seam_relief.kind: pocket in the lid underside (the lid stays closed from above)
lid_seam_relief.note: task I: the lid is closed over the front bay; over the bumper seam its underside is lifted by this pocket, so a rod pushed into the seam meets the sensed seam backer (and pushes it to its stop) before the fixed lid rim

spin_sweep.seam_end_land_note: Residual: an object thinner than the 7.5 mm seam that sits 2.7-3.9 mm inside the skin (r 155.0-156.2) meets the 1.2 mm radial land under the seam-end ramp when the robot spins: unsensed. Thinner land would not print (1.2 mm gate); listed in summary.residual_unsensed.

spin_sweep.verdict_rule: sensed only if the contact force (normal plus object friction mu along the slip) has a component >= 0.05 along the half travel; friction-limited contacts count as failures. The camera window edge faces (task F) are flagged camera_window_edge and must be sensed like any other face (their 62 deg flare gives the push along the travel).
spin_sweep.planar_play: pressed spin: the half skin is taken from its most outward planar-play pose at every travel
spin_sweep.controller_rule: A spin with a bumper pressed must stop (or reverse) before the pressed contact passes az ±90 deg; do not start a spin with an object within 6.4 mm outside the rear shell (r < 158.9) behind the axle.
spin_sweep.note: First face met by an object fixed in the world while the robot spins, starting from the free band behind the robot (r 152.5..158.9) and from the seam gap. Object friction mu 0.5 on the foam (az < 70), 0.2 on the PTFE-taped skin (az >= 70). The az ±78..90 tapers end at R152.7, outside the start of the rear shell (ramped from R151.5): an object leaving a pressed bumper end never meets a fixed face, and one coming from behind meets the ramp. The seam ends are 20 deg lead-in ramps, so an object crossing the seam pushes the other half.

fins.rule: >= 1.5 mm to every other part and wire; >= 6 deg from a foot rib

rear_shell.rib_scan_note: Per side, real hardware: hard = rib footprint vs rear cliff windows + ToF cones + under-base cliff screw heads, caster housing, tyres, countersunk Jetson standoff screw heads; plan = vs the lid-post feet (the deck-era saddle footprints), harness lanes and lid posts (z-separated); boss wall = Ø8 boss vs every other P_base hole (>= 1.5).

dowel.pad: 2 mm inner pad, 45 deg underside, around each dowel

bumper_clearance.state: planar play extremes (rest and hard stop, both halves)

camera_fov.note: Frusta from 0.5 mm in front of each apex to the floor; checked against every part including wires (lens excluded). Task F: the camera looks out through the bumper window (camera_window); the window keeps >= 4 mm to the lens-face frustum and >= 1.5 mm to the 3-mm-back one in every pose, including the planar-play extremes.

camera_window.print_support: a 1.8 mm plug at r 154.8..156.6 in each half (and a pillar under the right half upper seam backer) in the as-printed STL, cut out after printing
camera_window.rule: camera parts >= 1.5 mm from both halves (shell, foam, seam backer) at every travel and planar-play pose; lens recess >= hard-stop travel + 2 mm
camera_window.residual: An object small enough to pass the window opening (about 26 x 27 mm at the inner wall) can reach the lens without moving a half: the perimeter rods that do so are listed in rods_through_window. Anything larger meets a half first and trips it before the lens.

lidar_mount.method: Triangle samples of every part except the rotating turret, cap and windows, in z 123.5..131.5, outside r 30.2 about the spin axis.

min_range.note: front skin (R_SKIN) with a half at its hard stop (4.33 mm rearward, 2.5 mm inward) to the LiDAR spin axis; above 100 mm the LD14 sees an object the bumper touches

front_gap.rule: every LD14 part (housing, motor, turret, connector) stays >= 10 mm inside the bumper skin R_SKIN

caster_layout.front_support: none (user decision): the centre of mass sits behind the axle

stopping.reverse_speed_source: firmware reverse speed cap: the simulator firmware caps reverse at 0.06 m/s (the controller never commands more than 0.05 m/s in reverse); the rear-cliff coast check uses it
stopping.controller: DriveCore.h: a hazard disarms (tl = tr = 0); the wheels then see the simulator dynamic brake (coast)

if_reverse_were_not_capped.note: for information: without the firmware reverse cap a 0.15 m/s reverse would need this lead; the firmware cap is REQUIRED

active_brake_limit.note: DriveCore max_torque 0.1 N m per wheel caps any active brake at 1.63 m/s2; the coast is what the controller does today.

stopping.note: Latency = two VL53L0X timing budgets. Reflected axle inertia (0.0005 kg m2 per wheel) is in the effective mass for the coast and the torque-limited brake.

front.limitation: An edge met more obliquely than these angles, or driven along within 42 mm of a wheel, drops a wheel before a front sensor trips (the spec fixes the front sensors at (105, ±72)). Needs a controller rule (slow down near mapped edges) or outboard front sensors: user decision.

oblique_edges.rear: Rear sensors lead the caster by 35 + 81 tan(a): more for oblique edges.

spin_cliff_coverage.method: Straight edge at distance D from the axle; every start heading (0.5 deg) and both spin directions; unsafe when a wheel centre-plane (y ±114) crosses the edge before any cliff sensor has half its floor spot over it (zero stopping distance assumed: optimistic).
spin_cliff_coverage.limitation: Spinning in place next to an unmapped edge 104-113 mm from the axle can drop a wheel before any cliff sensor trips: the front sensors sit 56 deg from the wheel contacts. Needs a controller rule (no in-place spin near an unmapped edge after an oblique approach; back away first) or an extra sensor near az ±60-70 deg: user decision.

com_estimate.com_x_limit_source: user decision 2026-10-11 (task F): nominal <= -12 mm, every sensitivity case <= -10 mm (was -15 / -14), approved for an LD14 trial at x 109 and kept for x 54; every case keeps its 5 deg-downhill pitch onset >= 3 × the DriveCore braking ramp (0.25 m/s2). The simulator sync guard (COM_LIMIT_M) checks the same two limits.
com_estimate.braking_requirement: Keep forward braking below the pitch onset (level 2.64, 5 deg downhill 1.77 m/s2 nominal; 1.39 on the downhill in the worst sensitivity case): DriveCore ramps every wheel setpoint, braking included, at 0.25 m/s2 and a disarm coasts; its torque cap alone would allow about 1.63 m/s2, above that worst downhill onset, so keep the ramp in the firmware, never short-brake the motors (the driver coasts on disarm), and slow down on ramps.

placement.note: No ballast (user decision): the existing heavy parts sit as far aft as the layout allows.

battery.limit: tray rear wall flush with the rear base edge (x -124); P_base is 244 mm long on the 250 mm MK3S bed, so the base cannot grow aft

jetson.limit: NVIDIA B01 STEP turned +90 deg (I/O row forward, barrel jack on the right), on two 24 mm standoff stacks from P_base (front) and two 20 mm F-F standoffs on the bay board (rear, clamping it): carrier x -37..42. Its x was set in L1 by the COM sensitivity guard of that time (every case <= -14 mm): with the spec position (origin x 38, carrier x -24..55) the L1 model gave COM x -15.6 and -13.4 in the +50 g-forward case (a fail then); origin x 30 was the most forward that passed (-14.1), origin x 25 kept 0.5 mm of margin there. The rule now is the user's (task F, 2026-10-11): nominal <= -12 mm, every case <= -10 mm (com_x_limit_source); the Jetson has not moved. Bay board (B1): the Jetson stays at z 57; its rear standoffs clamp the board, whose under-carrier modules (DRV8874 × 2, GY-521) stay <= z 53.27. This build: COM x -16.1, worst case -13.64 (fill 1.0 and battery 10 % lighter).

placement.power_stage: bay board x -66.4..7.5 at base level under the Jetson, directly ahead of the battery tray (no room further aft); P03 turned 90 deg in the front bay (x 9..47) ahead of the board's tongue
placement.controller_lidar_camera: Task F: LD14 turned round, spin axis x 54, its 0.1 m blind circle inside the pressed bumper (user decision 2026-10-11, option B; COM rule relaxed to nominal <= -12 / worst <= -10 mm; the old spec x 20), camera lens face x 146 in the bumper window; the bumper halves (0.20 kg at x ~97) are the main forward mass

records.item: Controller and sensors: Pico and IMU on the bay board
Controller and sensors: bay board headers and input stages
Fasteners, inserts, pins, springs, bearings, races and balls (steel, CAD volume)

com_estimate.method: Printed: CAD volume × 1.27 g/cm3 × fill (mean wall 2V/A: 1.0 up to 3.0 mm, 0.62 from 3.6 mm = 2 × 4 perimeters × 0.45, linear in between) at the solid centroid. Bought: simulator record masses at CAD centroids (power stage and controller group spread over their parts). Steel from CAD volume. No ballast.

fill_model_check.note: Not part of the pass criterion: the step rule is what the previous rounds used. Under it the rear shells (mean walls just over 3.0 mm, printed with 4 perimeters, i.e. solid) drop to 62 %; weigh the printed shells to settle it.

threshold_crossing.model: Planar quasi-static: the driven wheels climb if mu >= tan(phi_edge) and their torque N R sin(phi) is within the cap; the free ball caster is lifted by an edge reaction through its centre (ball-housing friction ignored), carried by wheel traction (torque = traction R / 2 per wheel); pitch about the support on the floor; clearance from every body mesh vertex. Momentum, tyre compliance and slip dynamics ignored.

forward.clearance_point: lowest body point while the wheels are up (pitch about the caster), or the riser on the level approach
fails_because: rear caster cannot be dragged over (friction)
needs 0.307 N m per wheel, above the DriveCore cap 0.1 N m

reverse.clearance_point: lowest body point while the caster is up (pitch about the wheels), or the riser on the level approach
fails_because: needs 0.225 N m per wheel, above the DriveCore cap 0.1 N m

forward.clearance_point: lowest body point while the wheels are up (pitch about the caster), or the riser on the level approach
fails_because: drive wheels cannot climb the edge (friction)
rear caster cannot be dragged over (friction)
needs 0.567 N m per wheel, above the DriveCore cap 0.1 N m

reverse.clearance_point: lowest body point while the caster is up (pitch about the wheels), or the riser on the level approach
fails_because: drive wheels cannot climb the edge (friction)
lowest body point while the caster is up (pitch about the wheels), or the riser on the level approach strikes the floor
needs 0.266 N m per wheel, above the DriveCore cap 0.1 N m

capability_mm.note: largest square step (0.5 mm steps) not rated fail

threshold_crossing.motor_note: Pololu 4867 (99:1 MP 12 V) stall torque at 7.2 V is not in this package: the DriveCore cap 0.10 N m per wheel governs; verify the gearmotor rating before raising it.
options_for_user: 38 mm (r 19.05) caster ball: lowers the caster friction needed at 8-10 mm steps (needs a new caster and a lower mount)
raise or chamfer the bumper bottom edge at the front (z >= 23.5 for x > 140) for floor clearance when reversing over a step
raise the DriveCore torque cap after checking the gearmotor stall torque

lid_fan_window.note: Task L: the fan-window circle is the tray duct's circle about the fan centre; the lid has one opening round the whole duct (the window and motor circles + the 1.3 mm wall + 0.3 mm).

grille.slots: 5 × 5.2 mm on a 6.5 mm pitch inside r 17.5, no hub (task F: no lug tower over the fan); task L: the LD14 motor drops through a Ø26.4 hole in the plate, its 1.0 mm ring is open to the room

intake.over_grille: Room air through the grille and the 1.0 mm ring round the LD14 motor. Task L: the motor hangs in the intake duct, its rim 1.4 mm over the fan frame, and covers the bore's front edge: the motor's own footprint is not open area. 2.9 mm2 (0.5%) of the open area over the bore lies under the LD14 in plan, 2.9 mm2 of it the 1.0 mm ring round the motor; the gate counts that shadow as closed; those cells still draw air sideways over the plate, under the LD14 housing, through a curtain about 55 mm2 (4.0 mm clear over the plate × 13.8 mm across the window).
intake.method: plan shadow of the mesh triangles of every part above the fan top (tray, lid, fan and fan screws excluded) on the 0.25 mm grid over the bore; clear height = lowest overhanging surface over a shadowed open cell minus the plate top where that surface is above the plate (task L), else minus the fan top

fan_skirt.kind: intake duct under the LiDAR tray (task L; until then a skirt under the lid round the window): its fan-window circle r 17.5 and a circle r 13.2 round the LD14 motor, 1.3 mm wall; a bowl under the motor beyond the fan's front face

bowl_slot.rule: the bowl's back wall stays >= 0.5 mm in front of the fan's front face

fan_skirt.rule: bypass (wall gap × the duct's inner outline over the fan frame + the notches + the bowl slot + the LD14 lead aperture left open round its grommet) <= 25 % of the grille open area over the bore (CAD: through the plate, less the tray and the LD14 motor standing in its hole), with >= 1 % margin; the no-go feeler is under the gap at the limit; duct unbroken (section within 1 %); >= 0.5 mm to the fan screw heads and the fan's front face; the duct circle >= the fan bore; the LD14 motor >= 1.0 mm from the fan

jetson_cooling.bring_up_test: Lid-on load test before the robot is used: lid, LiDAR and tray fitted, sustained full CPU + GPU load for 20 min, log tegrastats (CPU/GPU/SoC temperatures and clocks) and compare with a lid-off run; the lid passes if the clocks never throttle. Carry into pcb/BRINGUP.md (L11).

exhaust.path: The fan blows down through the heatsink fins; the warm air leaves the body through the 2 mm ring gap between the bumper / rear-shell tops and the lid underside, the 7.5 mm bumper seam and the open ring between the base edge and the shells. Task I closed the lid over the front bay (until then an open notch of about 7050 mm2, left from the old camera tower): the ring gap alone stays several times the grille's open area.
exhaust.rule: the ring gap section (gap × circumference at the rear-shell rim's inner edge) >= 2 × the grille open area (CAD); the seam, the camera window and the base ring are extra

jetson_cooling.choice: The lid seams all meet near the centre (0, 0), which lies inside the fan footprint, so slots in the lid over the fan would cross them; so the grille is in the tray plate over the fan. The duct closes the 5.2 mm gap between the fan top and the lid, which would otherwise be a ~670 mm2 side inlet from inside the warm body. Task L: the lowered LD14's motor straddles the fan's front face, so the duct moved from the lid to the tray (one printed part, no joint) and takes the motor in, with a bowl under it beyond the fan.

lid_switches.rule: switch body bottom >= 10 mm over the battery top (z 64); >= 2 mm to the battery, the Tamiya pair, the straps and the bay board modules

rear_shell.rear_centre_note: At az 180 (between the ±155 deg gussets) the shell carries a push horizontally round the arc to the gussets (bending within the layers, not across them); the 10 mm top rim and the fins act as a ring beam.

motor_mount.note: The 45 deg gusset carries the root moment; beyond the gusset (y < 96) only the screw clamp load acts.

interlayer_stress.assumptions: Bumper: hit at z 87.5 or 98.5 at the 5 mm hard stop; 2 mm to trip, 10 ms latency, 2.0 m/s2 braking; series stiffness: EVA patch 450 N/mm and two 4 mm gussets in bending; the wall above a gusset tip acts over an 80 mm effective width of the 3.8 mm upper wall + 6 mm rim. cases[].consistent_stiffness is informational (the gate uses the model above): the foam is in series only for hits at or below its top (z 71.5; both hit heights are above it), and the wall above the gusset tip adds its own bending stiffness 3E(80 t^3/12)/(z_hit - 67.5)^3, E 2000 MPa; it is softer, so it gives a smaller force. Rear shell: 80 mm effective width at each foot-rib gusset, T-section with the fins inside that width. These are order-of-magnitude numbers: a printed half must pass the release proof test (50 N at z 98.5 into the stop, 5 cm drop).
interlayer_stress.mitigations: Bumper: 4 mm gussets to z 67.5 (rail) and 89.5 (arm), 3.8 mm upper wall; rear shell: 4 mm rib gussets to z 68 and 3 × 6 mm fins; 4 perimeters, ~245 °C, cooling <= 30 % below the rim; firmware speed cap 0.15 m/s; never lift by the shells.

limitations: Electronic envelopes and some mounting patterns remain assumptions; this is not a print-release or wiring-release check.
Friction-lock, Hertz, interlayer-stress, spin-sweep, coast and threshold-crossing results are quasi-static models; physical bump, tipping, stopping-distance, threshold and proof tests remain pending.

The camera window (task F) is open: an object small enough to pass it (about the size of the opening at the inner wall, camera_window.at_inner_wall) can reach the lens without moving a bumper half (camera_window.residual); anything larger trips the bumper first.
Spinning in place next to an unmapped edge 104-113 mm from the axle can drop a wheel before a cliff sensor trips (caster_layout.spin_cliff_coverage). User decision (controller rule or extra sensor).
Steps of 8 and 10 mm fail (threshold_crossing): the DriveCore torque cap and the 25.4 mm caster ball. User decision.
